title: EU boundary-aware routing decision graph with tenant safelisting
creator: Lena Park
description: Implement a deterministic decision graph and enforcement adapter that selects region, tier, and fallback model variants for requests subject to EU-only/data-residency constraints. This ticket focuses on the decision logic and tenant-level safelist/blocklist integration for cases where customers opt into alternative egress (e.g., partner-hosted EU region or approved non-EU fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Decision graph returns a canonical route (region + capacity tier + model variant) for all residency-tagged requests within unit tests
Tenant safelist/blocklist entries are checked with precedence rules and emergency passthrough disabled by default
Policy adapter emits structured telemetry (decision_id, reason_codes, matched_rules) to console-traces and audit logs
Fallback candidate ordering respects cost/latency tiers and legal constraints and is configurable per-customer
E2E test harness simulates EU-only tenant, tenant-with-safelisting, and tenant-with-blocking scenarios and asserts no non-EU egress unless explicitly safelisted
Rollout plan with canary flag and automatic kill-switch that reverts to safe-deny state on error rate or policy mismatches
implementation_notes: Build a small stateful decision-graph library (pure function API) that takes request metadata (tenant_id, residency_tags, requested_model, region_hint) and returns ordered route candidates
Add a thin adapter that consults TenantPolicyStore (existing) then applies safelist/blocklist precedence, emergency-override, and region-cap constraints
Ensure adapter calls are cheap: cache tenant policy for 5m, invalidate on policy change events
Expose hooks for console to preview computed route for a given request (no side-effects)
Model-variant naming: prefer explicit suffixes (e.g., model-7b-eu, model-7b-eu-fallback-quant) so runtime compatibility checks can be O(1)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Strict enforcement reduces functional surface for some customers who rely on cross-region fallbacks — we mitigate via tenant safelisting with audit trail
Caching tenant policies improves throughput but may delay emergency revocations; will add short TTL + push invalidation channel
Complex decision graphs increase cognitive load for on-call; provide a compact explanation in logs and a decision_id to tie to traces
test_plan: Unit: exhaustive decision-graph table-driven tests for combinations of residency_tags, tenant flags, and region hints
Integration: run routing adapter against a local policy store and a staged runtime to validate chosen host curves under load
Chaos: simulate policy-store latency and dropped invalidations to confirm fail-safe behavior (deny-by-default)
Perf: benchmark adapter at 20k rps with concurrent cache hits to ensure <2ms p50 overhead
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy adapter behind feature flag to 1% of EU traffic with decision logging enabled
Stage 2: expand to EU-only tenants with low traffic and manually validate audit logs
Stage 3: gradual ramp with automated checks on mismatched decisions and error budget triggers
Rollback: feature flag off, invalidate caches, and fail to safe-deny state
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if decision error rate > 0.1% for 5m
Alert on any audit-log write failures for residency decisions
Console dashboard: decision_id latencies, safelist match rate, blocked-request 5xx trends
